message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and depends on what you value—vocal technique, emotional depth, influence, or innovation. However, a few names consistently appear at the top of most lists:

| Singer | Why they’re often called the best |
|--------|-----------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and flawless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her deeply expressive voice and unique phrasing turned standards into personal statements; she’s a benchmark for emotional storytelling. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (trumpet & vocals) | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **Frank Sinatra** | His smooth phrasing and charismatic delivery made him a crossover icon while staying true to jazz roots. |
| **Nat King Cole** | A blend of jazz, pop, and blues, his warm baritone and impeccable timing earned him a lasting legacy. |

If you’re looking for a single “best,” many would argue **Ella Fitzgerald** because of her technical mastery and lasting influence on all subsequent jazz singers. But the beauty of jazz is that each of these artists offers a different flavor, so the “best” often comes down to personal taste.
